body: `auto` is [not allowed](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/contributing/development/cpp_usage_guidelines.html#auto-keyword)

This fragment is exactly repeated in `_animation_remove_confirmed()`. Perhaps it should be moved to a separate method like `_find_next_animation()`? Or, if we look at the larger fragment up to line 1276, we could move it along with the `UndoRedo` code, since they differ by two lines of code (the `UndoRedo` action name and getting the frame count).

This code fragment is repeated exactly (ignoring the difference in the blank line and `is_copy` field assignment) in `_animation_cut()`. It might make sense to create a static method `ClipboardAnimation::from_sprite_frames(const Ref<SpriteFrames> &p_frames, const String &p_anim, bool p_is_copy)`.

The naming convention regarding the `animation_` prefix is ​​a bit inconsistent. I'd prefer to either remove it or add it to all fields except `is_copy` (`frames` also belongs to animation, as do all other fields except `is_copy`).

I'm not sure the logic for clearing the buffer after pasting the cut animation is necessary. I couldn't find any other instances of `EditorSettings::get_singleton()->set_resource_clipboard(nullptr);`. In text editors, you can also paste the cut fragment an unlimited number of times.

After cutting or deleting the last animation, an error is displayed:

> ERROR: Animation '' doesn't exist.

It's not your fault, but we have to do something to fix it. CC @TokageItLab If I remember correctly, you once fixed a similar bug.
This field isn't used, it's only assigned. Personally, I'd prefer the original animation name to be used after insertion (plus a numeric suffix if one already exists).

This code incorrectly handles names like `name_subname`, where the last component isn't a number. Instead of adding the suffix `name_subname_2`, you get `name_1`. Also, as I noted in my previous comment, I personally would prefer that the pasted animation use the original name whenever possible (you save it, but don't use it), rather than using the name of the currently edited animation as a base.
But this code is used in `duplicate`; is it wrong there as well?

Yes, duplication also seems to be working incorrectly. Ideally, naming when duplicating animations should work the same way as when duplicating nodes with (the project setting `editor/naming/node_name_num_separator` set to "Underscore"). When inserting an animation, the mechanism is similar, but the original name must be taken as a basis, and not the name of the currently selected animation (you can compare it with inserting a node).
